steps.title: Ripe and jammy
steps.body: Zinfandel gives ripe, often jammy wines with blackberry, raspberry, bramble, black pepper and sweet spice, sometimes dried fruit. Alcohol is often high, 14.5 to 16%. Tannins are moderate, acidity medium. The style can range from light rosé to rich, powerful reds and sweet wines.

steps.title: Uneven ripening
steps.body: Zinfandel's bunches ripen unevenly: some berries are still green while others shrivel into raisins. Growers must wait for most to ripen, by which time some are overripe. That raises sugar and alcohol, and gives the mix of fresh and dried fruit flavours. It's also why picking time is so critical.
steps.highlight: Green berries and raisins on one bunch

steps.prompt: Why is Zinfandel often high in alcohol?
options: Uneven ripening means some berries shrivel and concentrate sugar
steps.explanation: Waiting for the green berries to ripen leaves others overripe, raising sugar and alcohol.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for medium to deep colour, ripe bramble and jammy berry fruit, black pepper and sweet spice, a warm, high-alcohol feel and moderate tannin. A hint of dried fruit or raisin is typical. It's fruitier and less tannic than Cabernet, spicier than Merlot.

steps.explanation: Zinfandel is medium to deep in colour, not pale.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Zinfandel gives ripe bramble fruit, spice and high alcohol
Uneven ripening mixes fresh and raisined berries
It ranges from rosé to rich red and sweet styles
